description: Rebuild public/index.html, public/app.js, and public/style.css implementing the 5-step SnapID workflow UI (Upload → Extract → Correct → Edit → Export) in vanilla HTML/CSS/JS. The old dashboard must remain accessible via a 'Switch to legacy batch view' back link. This feature is independent of FEAT-001 and FEAT-002 at build time (it is pure static frontend with no compile step), but depends on the API routes being in place at runtime.
steps: 1. Plan the frontend state machine before writing code. The app has two modes: 'snapid' (new 5-step flow) and 'legacy' (old dashboard). A top-level mode variable switches between them. Within snapid mode, a currentStep variable tracks 0=Upload, 1=Extract, 2=Correct, 3=Edit, 4=Export. Navigation is strictly forward with ability to go back to step 1 (re-upload) or restart. All snapid state lives in a plain JS object: { batchId, files: [], currentFileIndex, extractionResults: {}, correctionResults: {} }.

2. Rewrite public/index.html: Structure as a single-page app with two top-level sections: #snapid-app (the new flow, visible by default) and #legacy-app (the old dashboard, hidden by default). The legacy section contains the ENTIRE existing index.html content (setup card + dashboard card + all existing element IDs) copied verbatim — do not change any legacy element IDs. The snapid section contains: a header with the SnapID logo text and a 'Legacy batch view →' link; a step indicator bar (#step-bar) with 5 steps; and five step panels (#step-upload, #step-extract, #step-correct, #step-edit, #step-export) only one visible at a time.

   Step 1 panel (#step-upload): Large drag-and-drop zone accepting JPG/JPEG/PNG/HEIC individually, multiple, folder (webkitdirectory), and ZIP. File list preview. 'Start SnapID' button.

   Step 2 panel (#step-extract): Two-column layout. Left: original image thumbnail. Right: extraction result area with canvas overlay (#corner-canvas) for displaying/adjusting detected corners. Below: confidence badge, 'Adjust corners manually' toggle, 'Confirm & Continue' button, 'Previous file / Next file' navigation.

   Step 3 panel (#step-correct): A vertical progress list showing each processing stage (Face Detection, Alignment, Background Removal, Enhancement, Crop) with icons: pending ○, running ◎, done ✓, failed ✗. A 'Processing...' spinner. 'Retry' button on failure.

   Step 4 panel (#step-edit): Before/after side-by-side canvas comparison. Controls: background color picker (white/grey/light-blue/custom), zoom slider, horizontal pan, vertical pan, rotate slider (-5 to +5 deg), 'Reset to auto' button. 'Accept & Export' button.

   Step 5 panel (#step-export): Grid of result thumbnails. Per-file download link. 'Download all as ZIP' button (links to existing /api/batches/:id/export). 'Process more photos' restart button.

3. Write public/app.js as a single file ~600-900 lines. Sections: Section A — State & Helpers: const state = {mode:'snapid', step:0, batchId:null, files:[], currentFileIndex:0, extractionResults:{}, correctionResults:{}}; API helper reusing the existing api() pattern (fetch + error throw). Helper showStep(n) that hides all step panels and shows #step-{name}. Helper setMode(m) that toggles #snapid-app vs #legacy-app visibility and stores in localStorage. Section B — Legacy app bootstrap: Copy all existing app.js logic verbatim into this section, scoped to only run when mode==='legacy'. All existing element IDs still work because they exist inside #legacy-app. On mode switch to legacy, call the existing refresh() function. Section C — Step 1 Upload: Drag/drop + file input handlers. On 'Start SnapID': POST /api/batches to create a batch (settings: {useV2: true, ...defaults}). Then for each file, POST /api/batches/:id/upload. Transition to step 2 after all uploads complete. Section D — Step 2 Extract: For each file in sequence, call POST /api/files/:id/extract. Display the original via /api/files/:id/original in an . When extraction response arrives: if extracted_path exists, fetch /api/files/:id/preview and display in right panel. Draw detected corners on #corner-canvas as draggable circles. Confidence badge: green >= 0.7, yellow >= 0.5, red < 0.5. If confidence < 0.5, auto-show manual corner adjustment UI. 'Confirm & Continue': if corners were manually adjusted, POST /api/files/:id/confirm-crop with current canvas corner positions, then advance. Otherwise advance directly. Navigate all files before going to Step 3. Section E — Canvas corner selector: CornerSelector class. Constructor(canvas, imageElement). method setCorners(corners: [[x,y]x4]). method getCorners() -> [[x,y]x4]. Draws corner circles (radius 8, fill #16697a, stroke white). Handles mousedown/mousemove/mouseup for dragging individual corners. Scales corner coordinates between image display size and original pixel dimensions. Updates a dashed quadrilateral overlay connecting all 4 corners. Section F — Step 3 Correct: For each file that has an extractedPath, call POST /api/files/:id/correct. Poll GET /api/batches/:batchId every 1.5s to track state changes. Update stage progress list from result.stages dict. On all files completed/failed, advance to Step 4. Section G — Step 4 Edit: Load corrected image via /api/files/:id/download into a canvas. Load original extracted preview for before panel. Background picker: clicking a swatch re-calls POST /api/files/:id/correct with updated background color setting (optimistic UI). Zoom/pan/rotate sliders apply CSS transforms to the preview canvas (client-side only, for visual feedback — the actual correction re-call handles server-side). 'Reset to auto': restore sliders to defaults and reload. Section H — Step 5 Export: Query GET /api/batches/:batchId for all completed files. Render thumbnail grid. 'Download all' button links to /api/batches/:batchId/export.

4. Write public/style.css: Keep all existing CSS rules (they are needed by the legacy dashboard inside #legacy-app). Append new rules for the SnapID UI. New rules: #legacy-app { display: none } by default. body.legacy-mode #snapid-app { display: none }. body.legacy-mode #legacy-app { display: block }. Step bar: flex row, 5 items, active item highlighted in #16697a (matching existing brand color). Step panels: display:none by default, display:block when active. Corner canvas: position:absolute, overlaid on the image preview container with pointer-events:all. Stage progress list: flex column, each item has icon + label + status. Before/after comparison: side-by-side flex with labels. Background swatches: 4 colored circles + custom color input. Export grid: CSS grid 4 columns, each cell with thumbnail + filename + download link. All new colors use the existing palette (#16697a teal, #14a098 accent, #17212b text, #f4f6f8 background, #dde4e8 border).
acceptance_criteria: public/index.html contains both #snapid-app and #legacy-app sections; all existing legacy element IDs (batchName, headline, rows, progress, etc.) are preserved inside #legacy-app
public/app.js CornerSelector class exists and handles mousedown/mousemove/mouseup drag
Clicking 'Legacy batch view' link switches mode and shows the old dashboard
Step navigation progresses Upload → Extract → Correct → Edit → Export
public/style.css retains all original CSS and adds SnapID-specific rules without breaking legacy styles
verification: npm run build — must exit 0 (frontend has no compile step but server.ts imports nothing from public/; this confirms the Node side still compiles)
Manual smoke-test: open http://localhost:3000 in a browser — SnapID upload step is shown; clicking 'Legacy batch view' shows the old dashboard with 'New batch' button
